1 Workflow Summary

Below is a narrative, step-by-step account of the CellChat analysis recorded in Assignment2_CellChat.qmd. The bullets are distilled from the code, in-line comments, and annotations inside the notebook.

  • Working directory & scaffolding
    The script sets root.directory, then creates the figures, tables, and checkpoints folders so that outputs are cleanly organised and can be reproduced by any one.

  • Library loading
    CellChat, patchwork, and Seurat are loaded.

  • Seurat object import
    The annotated object seu_with_SingleR.rds is read in; a quick table(seu$SingleR_label) confirms 3789 cells across 13 cell types (small clusters such as CMP and Neurons are present).

  • CellChat object construction
    Cells are grouped by SingleR_label and converted with createCellChat(). The human ligand–receptor database is attached and restricted to secreted signalling genes.

  • Pre-processing & probability inference
    Over-expressed genes/interactions are identified (437 LR pairs) before computing communication probabilities. Clusters with <10 cells (e.g. CMP, Neurons) are filtered out leading to~77% of low-confidence interactions being discarded at this step.

  • Pathway-level aggregation
    Communication probabilities are collapsed into pathway scores via computeCommunProbPathway() and aggregateNet(); centrality metrics are computed with netAnalysis_computeCentrality().

  • Visualization
    Circle, heatmap, scatter, bubble, and violin plots are generated, each called with remove.isolate = TRUE so that low‑cell groups already discarded by filterCommunication() do not appear in the graphics, and written to write/figures/ (see Section 2).

  • Exporting results
    All intermediate tables are exported to write/tables/, figures to write/figures/, and the CellChat object is saved as checkpoints/cellchat.rds.

3 Biological interpretation of tumor-promoting pathways

MIF (Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor)

  • Tumor-promoting context: MIF–CD74 signalling polarizes macrophages toward an M2 phenotype, dampening cytotoxic T-cell function and fostering angiogenesis.

  • Evidence here: Figure CC-5/6 reveal robust T <> macrophage and B <> macrophage MIF exchange, suggesting an immunosuppressive loop.

GALECTIN (LGALS9)

  • Tumor‑promoting context: Galectin‑9 engagement of receptors such as CD44 and the immune‑checkpoint adaptor CD45 attenuates T‑cell activation, promotes immune evasion, and supports fibroblast‑mediated matrix remodelling. Interaction with P4HB has been linked to enhanced extracellular‑matrix deposition and tumour invasion.

  • Evidence here: Figures CC‑7/8 show a monocyte‑centred Galectin‑9 network targeting CD44, CD45 and P4HB on NK, T and B cells, indicating stromal remodelling and checkpoint‑like suppression.

3.0.1 Contribution of key stromal/immune compartments

Cell type Observed role in this dataset
Macrophages Central senders & receivers in both MIF and GALECTIN pathways; likely orchestrate an M2-like, tumour-supportive niche.
Fibroblasts (not captured as a separate label) The GALECTIN axis suggests fibroblast-like signalling activity via CD44, supporting ECM deposition and immune exclusion.
Plasma cells / B-cells Act as prominent MIF senders to macrophages, potentially enhancing immunosuppression.
